tool_plan.objective: Generate representative Chrome web-cache content through browser use, then preserve the Chrome cache for ChromeCacheView parsing and export validation.

required_actions.name: browser.launch
required_actions.why: Starts the Chromium profile whose cache ChromeCacheView can read.

required_actions.name: browser.goto
required_actions.why: Loads distinct web documents and their cacheable resources.

required_actions.name: browser.get_clickables
required_actions.why: Discovers visible controls and meaningful navigation or form targets.

required_actions.name: browser.click
required_actions.why: Exercises observed links or controls that load additional cacheable content.

required_actions.name: browser.smart_type
required_actions.why: Creates search or form-request variations that can produce distinct cached responses.

required_actions.name: browser.scroll
required_actions.why: Reveals lazy-loaded or progressive content that may add cache entries.

required_actions.name: browser.screenshot
required_actions.why: Preserves visible-state evidence for content corresponding to generated cache entries.

required_actions.name: browser.close
required_actions.why: Closes the browser after activity so pending cache data can be flushed before collection.

completion.detail: Complete only after the browser has been closed and Chromium cache data is present for collection and parsing by ChromeCacheView.

tool_plan.action_intent_guidance: Action Flow: Launch the Chromium profile, then use run-provided runtime targets with browser.goto to load a few distinct, naturally resource-rich pages. On each relevant page, use browser.get_clickables to observe currently visible links, navigation, search, or form controls; use browser.click and browser.smart_type only on observed, relevant controls to request additional visible content and response variants. Use browser.scroll to reveal progressive or lazy-loaded resources, then re-run browser.get_clickables after the newly visible state appears; keep this observe -> reveal -> re-observe loop bounded. Capture browser.screenshot when visible page state supports the browsing activity that populated cache entries. Visit additional runtime-provided targets as appropriate, then use browser.close to flush pending cache writes, producing chromium.cache.cache_data. Reason guidance: write context-specific reasons that state the action and cache effect, such as loading a resource-rich page, following an observed content link, submitting an observed search variation, or revealing lazy-loaded content to populate additional cache entries.
